bull.b: Closing the Sobi partnership and initiating TELLOMAK-3 converts lacutamab into a funded late-stage development program. The $75 million upfront payment and expected runway through Q1 2028 provide execution time, while potential milestones and royalties add longer-term optionality.

Lacutamab's FDA breakthrough and fast track designations, EMA PRIME status, and orphan designations support regulatory engagement in a defined rare-disease setting. These designations can facilitate development and reinforce the program's strategic relevance as Phase 3 advances.

Internal capabilities are being used to build multiple next-generation ADC approaches, including dual-targeted bispecifics, enhanced internalization, and dual-payload designs. A broader platform can diversify the pipeline beyond one asset and create additional opportunities for future clinical development.

bear.b: Revenue fell about 48% in 2025 after higher 2022–2023 levels, while operating losses and net margins remained deeply negative. This combination shows the current revenue base is not yet supporting the cost structure, limiting evidence of durable operating leverage over the next several quarters.

Shareholders’ equity turned negative in 2025 after a stronger 2020–2023 equity base. The erosion from cumulative losses reduces financial flexibility and leaves the company more exposed to solvency pressure, dilution, or refinancing needs as clinical programs continue.

Operating and free cash flow were negative in every year shown, including roughly $50.7 million of operating outflow in 2025. Persistent cash burn means the company is not self-funding and must continue relying on external capital to sustain development.
